chebyshev_coeffs_nd — MATH numerics op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.chebyshev_coeffs_nd(values, box=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import mathnumerics; mathnumerics.chebyshev_coeffs_nd(values, box=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsmath.get("chebyshev_coeffs_nd"))

Usage

Computes N-dimensional Chebyshev coefficients from values sampled on a tensor-product Chebyshev–Lobatto grid (DCT-I).

Args:

values: array of shape (n1, …, nd). The samples on axis i are the values on chebyshev_nodes(n_i, lo_i, hi_i) (ascending).

box: interval per axis [(lo, hi), …] (if omitted, [−1, 1] on all axes; 1 pair is shared by all axes).

Returns:

coeffs (n1, …, nd): f ≈ Σ c[k] Π T_{k_i}(t_i) (t_i is the coordinate mapped to [−1, 1]), box,

decay = per axis, the max of |c| listed by degree (for smooth functions it falls geometrically = spectral convergence),

tail = per axis, the max of |c| over the last 2 degrees (a gauge of truncation error; the smaller, the more sufficient the number of points).

Gate: polynomials of degree at most n_i − 1 on each axis are reproduced exactly / for functions with a pole of the form 1/(a − x), the coefficients fall as ρ^−k (ρ = a + √(a² − 1), Bernstein ellipse). For images, smooth surfaces such as uneven illumination or warping are represented with a few dozen coefficients (the polynomial power basis is ill-conditioned at high degree; Chebyshev is stable).

Family-wide input contract (fail-closed)

Every mathops op validates its input before computing (nothing slips through silently):

• complex input raises ValueError — coercing to float64 silently discards the imaginary part (numpy only emits a ComplexWarning and returns a plausible-looking wrong real number). State .real/.imag/abs() explicitly, or use complexops, which handles complex data.

• masked arrays with masked elements raise ValueError — the implicit conversion that peels off the mask and uses the raw values underneath is refused. Say explicitly whether to fill or to drop.

• NaN/Inf raises ValueError on every input (refused with the count stated — it propagates through the whole result).

• Shapes are strict: 1-D and 2-D are never implicitly promoted or broadcast (a matrix in a vector slot, or a vector in a matrix slot, raises ValueError; reshape explicitly).

• Size cap: ops that take a matrix, and the stat_histogram bins, raise ValueError beyond mathops.MAX_ELEMENTS (2^26 ≈ 67 million elements).
